errors.text: The hypothesis substitutes an oxidizing, macroscopic reciprocating-wear experiment for the target nanoindentation/friction simulation, where protective tribo-oxide formation is not part of the modeled mechanism.
It replaces the FeNiCrCoCu coating on single-crystal Cu with materially different Al-containing or refractory HEA systems.

It predicts improved wear resistance and decreasing friction with temperature, whereas the target has approximately stable hardness and wear resistance through 600 K, followed by sharp softening and increased, strongly fluctuating friction above about 900 K.

The proposed precipitate-coarsening and oxide-spallation degradation mechanism is not established by the cited evidence; E4 explicitly reports no coarsening and only supports beneficial high-temperature oxidation.
